result:
I've written the design for experiment 19 to `runs/pending_experiment.json`. It swaps each of the two committee members' MobileNetV2 feature extractor for an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0, and nothing else changes.

**Why this experiment:**
- **Only the extractor has moved the held-out 2024 photograph.** Each upgrade of the pretrained extractor lifted usable fixes, from 10.75% (exp 11) to 49.5% (exp 12), 60% (exp 13), 65.5% (exp 14), 74% (exp 15) and 86.75% (exp 16). Exp 18's ring pooling left the extractor alone and finished level with the champion (0.158 vs 0.155).
- **The rest of the score is the survey gap, mostly abstentions.** On the three training photographs exp 16 is 100% usable with 0% false fixes. On 2024, 11% of frames fall below the 0.3 confidence threshold, while the frames it does answer are 97.5% right. More survey-invariant features should turn those abstentions into fixes.
- **EfficientNet-B0 is the strongest openly licensed option that fits.** It scores 77.7% on ImageNet (MobileNetV2: 71.9%). Its two output depths have the same grid sizes and strides as the two the current design reads (14×14 and 7×7), so no other stage needs to change.

**Prediction:** mission score 0.155 → about 0.09–0.12, usable about 89–92%, false fixes flat at about 2–2.5%. If usable stays at or below 87.5%, a stronger pretrained extractor has stopped paying off, and the next lever is the training data or signal.

**Risk to watch:** model size. My estimate puts the exported model at about 30.1 MiB against the 32 MiB gate. The same arithmetic matches exp 16's measured 17.39 MB, but the margin is small. The brief has the implementation agent export an untrained model and check its size first, and stop and report rather than shrink anything if it's over. It also has to bake the new weights file (`model/pretrained/effb0_features7.pt`) so remote training can ship it, and run a smoke test that catches the kind of missing-import crash that killed exp 17. Training will take roughly 1.3–1.8× as long as exp 16.
